national_news.title: Supreme Court to Form Committee on Delhi Student Protests
bullets: The Supreme Court announced the formation of a high-powered committee comprising retired apex court and high court judges, a former DGP, and an ex-CBI director.
The panel will examine allegations of police excesses against student protesters and violence against police personnel during the July 20 Parliament march in Delhi.
The committee will also investigate allegations of sexual assault, online harassment, and the victimisation of vulnerable persons.

national_news.title: 12th BRICS Environment Ministers Meeting Held in New Delhi
bullets: Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav presided over the 12th BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
The theme of India’s BRICS Chairship 2026 is 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'.
India highlighted that it reduced pollution emission intensity by over 37 percent between 2005 and 2022, with more than half of its power capacity now from clean sources.

national_news.title: BWF Badminton World Championships: Unnati Hooda Advances
bullets: India’s Unnati Hooda advanced to the women’s singles second round at the BWF Badminton World Championships held at Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium, New Delhi.
She defeated Myanmar’s Thet Htar Thuzar in straight games (22-20, 21-16).
She advanced to face the 13th-seeded Michelle Li of Canada in the Round of 32.

national_news.title: News Services Division of All India Radio: Structure and Broadcast Profile
bullets: The News Services Division (NSD) of All India Radio (AIR) operates 24X7 under the motto 'Bahujan Hitaya, Bahujan Sukhaya', headed by a Director General (News).

Historical milestones include the first news bulletin broadcast from Bombay on July 23, 1927, followed by Calcutta in August 1927, before coming under direct Government control and being renamed All India Radio on June 8, 1936.
AIR currently broadcasts 607 daily news bulletins spanning 3,150 minutes across 92 languages and dialects, including foreign languages like Arabic, Burmese, French, and Tibetan.

national_news.title: Akashwani Annual Awards Guidelines and Categories
bullets: The News Services Division of AIR issues annual guidelines for prestigious honors including the K. L. Sharma Award for Best Correspondent.
Other recognized categories under the Akashwani Annual Awards include the Best PTC (Piece to Camera) Award and the Best Newsreader Award.
These awards acknowledge and honor excellence in radio broadcasting, reporting, and news reading standards.

national_news.title: Constitutional Structure of India's Legislature and Executive Leadership
bullets: The Rajya Sabha (Upper House) has a sanctioned strength of up to 250 members (238 from States/UTs and 12 nominated by the President) with members serving staggered six-year terms.
The Lok Sabha (Lower House) has a maximum constitutional capacity of 550 members, currently comprising 542 elected members based on universal adult suffrage for a five-year term.
Key constitutional functionaries highlighted include the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Governors, Chief Ministers, and Supreme Court Judges.

national_news.title: PIB Dehradun Organises Regional Media Workshop 'Vartalaap' in Chamoli
bullets: Press Information Bureau (PIB) Dehradun organized the regional media workshop 'Vartalaap' in Gopeshwar, Chamoli district on August 20, 2026.
The workshop targets print, electronic, and digital media professionals in rural and border areas to build awareness about central welfare schemes, GI tags, and ODOP.
Vartalaap serves as a flagship outreach program by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting to bridge the gap between government initiatives and grassroots communication.

national_news.title: Indian Army Contingent Departs for India-Thailand Joint Military Exercise MAITREE-XV
bullets: The 15th edition of India-Thailand Joint Military Exercise MAITREE-XV (2026) is being conducted from August 18 to 31, 2026, at Vibhavadi Rangsit Camp, Surat Thani, Thailand.
Both Indian Army (represented primarily by the 9 Gorkha Rifles) and Royal Thai Army contingents comprise 85 personnel each.
Instituted in 2006, the exercise focuses on joint counter-insurgency and counter-terrorist operations in jungle and semi-urban environments under Chapter VII of the United Nations Charter.

national_news.title: UDISE+ 2025-26 Report Highlights School Education Progress
bullets: The UDISE+ Report 2025-26 covers 14.67 lakh schools, 1.03 crore teachers, and 24.72 crore students across India.
The overall Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) stands at 24:1, comfortably within the NEP 2020-recommended benchmark of 30:1.
The Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) at the Secondary stage improved to 71.7%, while the Middle stage GER stood at 89.6%.

national_news.title: Ministry of Defence Signs Rs 1,943 Crore Deal to Lease MQ-9B Sea Guardian Drones
bullets: The Ministry of Defence signed a contract with General Atomics Aeronautical Systems for leasing two MQ-9B Sea Guardian HALE RPAS for the Indian Navy.
The lease contract is valued at approximately Rs 1,943 crore for a period of 30 months.
The drones will significantly enhance the Indian Navy's Maritime Domain Awareness capabilities and provide persistent ISR coverage over the Indian Ocean Region.

national_news.title: Security Agencies Bust ISI-backed Shahzad Bhatti Network in Multi-State Crackdown
bullets: Indian security agencies detained 253 people across 14 states in a coordinated operation against the ISI-backed Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN).
Over 80 FIRs and 200+ arrests have been recorded against SBN under provisions including UAPA, BNS, and the Arms Act.
Substantial recoveries include IEDs, Pakistan Ordnance Factory-marked grenades, pistols, and CCTV cameras used for espionage.

national_news.title: Department of Financial Services Hosts PSB Confluence 2026
bullets: The two-day PSB Confluence 2026 was organised by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance.
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced that a high-powered Committee on Banking Reforms for Viksit Bharat will be announced soon.
Day 1 deliberations focused on four key themes: Deposit Mobilisation, Banking for Youth, Supporting the Investment Cycle, and Global Capability Centres (GCCs).

national_news.title: India Leads Global Areca Nut Production in 2025-26 DASD Report
bullets: India is the world's largest producer of areca nut (betel nut), accounting for about 63% of total global production in 2025-26 according to the DASD report.
The area under arecanut cultivation increased to 11.06 lakh hectares, with total production estimated at 15.29 lakh tonnes.
Karnataka is the largest producing state in India, contributing around 10 lakh tonnes of the total output.

national_news.title: Centre Approves Rs 1,419 Crore for Qadian-Beas Railway Line in Punjab
bullets: The Centre approved a detailed estimate of Rs 1,419.05 crore for the 39.68 km Qadian-Beas broad-gauge railway line in Punjab's Majha region.
The project will connect Qadian in Gurdaspur district with Beas in Amritsar district, executed by Northern Railway.
Infrastructure plans include two crossing stations, 11 major bridges, 121 minor bridges, 54 Road Under Bridges (RUBs), and the deployment of the Kavach train collision avoidance system.

national_news.title: India-EU FTA and CBAM Compliance Challenges
bullets: The EU and India concluded Free Trade Agreement (FTA) negotiations in January 2026, coinciding with the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) entering its definitive financial phase.
Differences in how India and the EU measure and recognize carbon costs risk imposing a double compliance burden on Indian exporters.
The challenge highlights the need for harmonizing domestic emissions regulations with EU's carbon-sensitive trade frameworks to protect trade gains.

bihar_news.title: Study Highlights Need for Smallholder-Centric Carbon Credit Programmes in India
bullets: India accounts for around 4.1 percent of the global voluntary carbon market, but smallholder participation remains limited despite comprising over 80 percent of farmers.
A study involving smallholder farmers in Bihar identified upfront financial support and technical training as the most critical determinants for participation.
The Green Credit Programme and Indian Carbon Market initiative are key government frameworks promoting sustainable practices and emissions reduction.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Joins Centre's Direct Pulse Procurement Network for the First Time
bullets: In a first, Bihar has joined the Centre's direct pulse procurement network, enabling central agencies to procure masoor directly from farmers bypassing the absence of APMC mandis.
NCCF and Nafed have procured around 3,000 tonnes of masoor against a target of 32,000 tonnes, benefiting about 750 farmers at an MSP of ₹7,000 per quintal.
Bihar produces nearly 400,000 tonnes of pulses annually across approximately 448,000 hectares of cultivated land.

bihar_news.title: Darbhanga Ranks Second in Bihar for Sugarcane IDs
bullets: Darbhanga has emerged as Bihar’s second-highest district in obtaining Sugarcane IDs, with 24,215 farmers joining the sugarcane expansion campaign.
West Champaran holds the first rank in Bihar for the number of farmers with Sugarcane IDs.
The Sugarcane ID connects farmers with departmental schemes, technical support, and government incentives to boost cultivation and supply to sugar mills.

bihar_news.title: Bihar to Resume Mining Operations from October 15, Announces CM Samrat Choudhary
bullets: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary inaugurated the auction of critical and strategic mineral blocks and the NMEDT workshop organized by the Ministry of Coal and Mines in Patna.
The state government announced that more than 30 of the 44 surveyed coal blocks will be allocated before September 30, with mining operations officially set to begin on October 15.
Key mineral reserves identified across districts include limestone in Rohtas, mineral belts in Aurangabad, magnets in Jehanabad and Jamui, and significant resources in Gaya, Banka, and Bhagalpur.

bihar_news.title: Bihar Govt Highlights Key Developmental Projects and Administrative Portals
bullets: The Gaya Integrated Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) will have road and water infrastructure completed before 2027, with plans to channel water from the Sone river to the Falgu river.
The newly introduced 'Vidyarthi Sahyog Portal' aims to eliminate student grievances and bring transparency and accountability to the state's education system.
Plans are underway for the construction of a World Trade Center in Patna to boost trade, industry, and economic activities.
